fieldMarks: Two black collars around the neck enclosing a lighter collar; olive-brown to gray body with many lighter spots that continue onto the tail in a reticulated pattern; white or light belly (NDOW).
No black pigment lining the mouth, unlike C. collaris (NatureServe).
Adult males: strongly laterally compressed tail with a pale white dorsal stripe, enlarged dark inguinal patches, and a pale, patternless top of the head (NatureServe).
Gravid females have orange spots on the sides (NDOW).
behavior: Perches on rocks; when startled hides under rocks or in rodent burrows; very fast and can run on hind legs alone (NDOW).
Breeding males are territorial, bobbing from a rock and extending a blue and black throat dewlap (NDOW).
Eats insects, spiders, other lizards and some plant material (NDOW; NatureServe).
Inactive in cold winter weather; activity begins as early as March in Arizona (NatureServe).
habitat: Xeric, sparsely vegetated rocky areas: hillsides, rocky plains and canyons; sometimes adjacent areas with little rock (NDOW; NatureServe).
range: Southeastern Oregon and southern Idaho south through northeastern California, Nevada, and western and central Utah to southeastern California and western Arizona (NatureServe).

lookalikes.name: Eastern collared lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Eastern collared lizard has a black-lined mouth; Great Basin lacks oral melanin (NatureServe; CPW).

lookalikes.name: Baja California collared lizard
lookalikes.howToTell: Baja California collared lizard has widely separated posterior collars and slender white transverse dorsal bars (NatureServe).
